content.title: 2025 Chicago Marathon: Preview, full schedule, and how to watch the 47th edition live
content.text: Athletes to watch at the 2025 Chicago Marathon Defending champion John Korir returns as Jacob Kiplimo seeks history in his second marathon Kelvin Kiptum may be gone, but he is not forgotten. He remains the fastest man in history, and the 2:00:35 he spent on Chicago's streets that Sunday morning in October 2024 continue to resonate through marathon history, particularly in the American city where he achieved the feat. When the elite men, led by the defending champion Korir, embark on the world-record course this year, they will endeavour to emulate the late Kiptum and secure their place in the race's hall of fame. Korir, 27, won his first World Marathon Major with a 2:02:44 run that made him the eighth-fastest man in history. He began his season with a bang, securing his fourth career marathon victory by winning the Boston Marathon. He is the presumptive favourite and aims to replicate the feat of his compatriot, the late Samuel Wanjiru, who achieved back-to-back titles in 2010. The Kenyan wants to beat his own personal best. while Kiplimo, who is running only his second marathon, will likely be chasing him. At the 2025 London Marathon, the Ugandan finished in second place, behind Sabastien Sawe. Furthermore, Kiplimo, who is only 23 years old, holds the world record for the half marathon. The other sub-2:03 runner in the field is Timothy Kiplagat. The 32-year-old has been in excellent form since he transitioned to a marathon after spending much of his late teens and early 20s working odd jobs while consuming locally brewed spirits. His most notable accomplishment was at the Tokyo 2024 marathon, where he secured the second spot. The US challenge is led by Paris 2024 Olympian Mantz, who is targeting Khalid Khannouchi’s American record of 2:05:38 from 2022. “I want to get the American record. I’m well prepared. On the right day, you can do something pretty special in Chicago,” Mantz, who was eighth in the Olympic race, told the organisers. “After Boston, where I finished with guys who have run 2:02 and 2:03, it doesn’t feel like a stretch to say I can run 2:05:30 on a looped, flat course.”Who will be the new women's Chicago marathon champ? A new women’s champion will be crowned on Sunday, with defending champion Ruth Chepng’etich, who shattered the world record last year, serving a doping ban. Ethiopia presents a formidable line-up, led by debutant Hawi Feysa, a 2:17:00 runner, and her compatriot Megertu Alemu, who finished third in the 2023 edition and is the reigning Valencia Marathon winner. “I look forward to returning to the Chicago Marathon to try and improve on my previous performance there,” said Alemu. “The course is very flat and fast; and with my good training this year; I feel that I am fit to run better this time in Chicago and move higher up.” Other seasoned marathoners include Irine Cheptai, who rounded off last year's podium, and Mary Ngugi-Cooper, who is seeking her first win on the US soil after six previous attempts in Boston. Dakotah Popehn leads the American field. In the wheelchair divisions, defending champions Switzerland’s Catherine Debrunner and Marcel Hug will be on the starting line at Grant Park. Debrunner is chasing her third consecutive win in Chicago, while the Swiss 'silver bullet' is tipped to claim his seventh win.2025 Chicago Marathon schedule Sunday, 12 October The Chicago Marathon, which has drawn over 53,000 participants from more than 100 countries, will begin at 7:20 a.m. (US Central Time) with the wheelchair races, followed by the elite runnerst to start at 7:30 a.m. The start and finish line is at Grant Park. 2025 Chicago Marathon Start times: All local timings which is UTC/GMT -6 7:20 a.m.: Marathon Wheelchair start (men) 7:21 a.m.: Marathon Wheelchair start (women) 7:23 a.m.: Marathon Handcycle start 7:30 a.m.: Wave 1 start (Elite & Corrals A, B, C, D and E) 8:00 a.m.: Wave 2 start (Corrals F, G, H and J) 8:35 a.m.: Wave 3 start (Corrals K, L, M and N) How to watch the 2025 Chicago Marathon Olympic Channel will have live broadcast and digital streaming coverage of the race in selected territories including Japan, via Olympics.com and the official Olympics app. In the US, NBC 5 Chicago and Telemundo Chicago will provide live coverage from 7 a.m. – 11 a.m. (US Central Time). In Mexico the 2025 Chicago Marathon will be streamed on Peacock and Roku from 7 a.m. to 3 p.m. (US Central Time), as well as on nbcchicago.com and telemundochicago.com and the NBC Chicago and Telemundo Chicago apps. International viewers can watch the race via a variety of global broadcast partners, including Eurosport, Eurosport India, SMG China, FloSports, ESPN Brazil and ESPN Latin America.
